title: The Renewal of Creation and of Man
english: For He is also the giver of the good things we expect to come. He will refashion creation and renew the whole universe, and He will set it free from slavery into the freedom of the glory of the children of God (Romans 8:21). And if this is true, how could it not be wholly necessary that the one for whose sake creation exists, I mean man, should be renewed together with creation?

Man too had to be seen as new: not tyrannized by the first corruption, not overpowered by fleshly pleasures into sins, but raised instead in incorruption, in strength and in honor, and clothed with a divine glory (1 Corinthians 15:42–43). For the inspired Isaiah also says somewhere, “Your righteousness shall go before you, and the glory of God shall clothe you” (Isaiah 58:8).

And indeed our Lord Jesus Himself plainly affirmed that at the time of the end of this age the dead will come back to life (Matthew 13:40–43; Daniel 12:2), but “those who understand will shine like the brightness of the firmament” (Daniel 12:3). Yet the grace of such honor and glory will not be set before all without distinction. It would rather befit those who have been chosen out from the rest, who have also been conformed to the image of His Son (Romans 8:29).
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 74, Fragmenta in 1 Cor (Khazarzar transcription). Original English from the Greek; no English base used.

The section opens with ‘διανομεὺς ἀγαθῶν’, the end of a sentence begun in the previous section (‘αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστι καὶ τῶν ἔσεσθαι προσδοκωμένων’); the previous section ends before that sentence, so the whole of it (‘For He is also the giver of the good things we expect to come’) is rendered here.
The section ends inside the quotation of Romans 8:29 (‘σύμμορφοι … τῆς’); ‘εἰκόνος τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ’ opens the Greek of the next section and is rendered here so the sentence is whole.
The printed punctuation ‘διεβεβαιοῦτο· σαφῶς, ὡς’ is read as ‘διεβεβαιοῦτο σαφῶς ὡς’ (‘plainly affirmed that’).

The quoted words come from Daniel 12:3, but Cyril attributes the saying to the Lord, joining it to Matthew 13:40–43 (the end of the age, the righteous shining). Both are cited; the attribution is kept as he gives it.
ἀπολέγδην (‘by selection’) with τοῖς τῶν ἄλλων ἐξῃρημένοις is rendered ‘those who have been chosen out from the rest’; the Greek implies no number.
